description:
You are the Third-Party Risk Manager at First National Capital Bank, a mid-size regional bank with $18B in assets under management. Following the 2023 MOVEit supply chain breach that compromised data at hundreds of financial institutions — including several of First National's peer institutions — your Chief Risk Officer has mandated a comprehensive Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program.

Your immediate charter: formally register all critical vendors in Eramba, document the key risk exposures each vendor introduces, establish governing policy, and begin tracking the quarterly assessment cycle.

Complete ALL of the following in Eramba (credentials at /home/ga/eramba/credentials.txt):

1. Register at least 4 new critical third-party vendors not already in the system (AWS and Salesforce are already registered). Examples of vendors to add: FIS Global (core banking platform), Experian (credit bureau and KYC/AML data), Jack Henry & Associates (digital banking and payment rails), and Symitar (credit union and lending system). The bank's actual vendors may vary — you should register 4 vendors that are plausible critical suppliers for a regional bank.

2. For each new vendor, create at least one risk that the vendor relationship introduces (e.g., vendor concentration risk, supply chain attack, SLA breach causing business continuity failure, third-party data breach exposing customer PII). Each of these 4+ risks must have a treatment strategy set.

3. Create a security policy titled 'Third-Party Risk Management Policy' with status 'Approved'. This policy must govern how the bank manages and monitors all vendor relationships.

4. Create a project with 'Vendor' in the title to track the first round of vendor risk assessments (e.g., 'Q2 Vendor Risk Assessment Program').

5. Create at least 2 policy exceptions for vendors that cannot yet meet the bank's full TPRM requirements (e.g., a legacy data provider with an expiring SOC 2 report, a fintech partner pending security questionnaire completion).
